title: POC Weekly Sync - Reliability incident followup
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on the reliability incident last week: increased 5xxs and timeouts during peak traffic. Reviewed initial logs, hypothesized causes (autoscaling gap, retry storm, gateway timeouts), and agreed on immediate mitigations and investigation plan. Next steps include sharing full trace logs, running controlled load repro, and a patch to client-side retry/backoff and rate limit tuning.
topics: Retry/backoff behavior and client SDK config
action_items: Ethan Park - collect and share aggregated server logs (nginx/gateway + model runtime) including 5xx traces and latencies - due: 2026-03-31
Priya Singh - export traffic spike CSV and sample payloads from 2026-03-25 18:00 to 19:30 (UTC) - due: 2026-04-02
Maya Thompson - send updated POC runbook with recommended client retry/backoff config and temporary rate-limit policy - due: 2026-03-30
Laura Chen - coordinate a 30-min controlled repro window next week (preferred: 2026-04-01 14:00-14:30 PT) - due: 2026-03-30
next_steps: Redwood to provide granular 5xx root-cause notes + suggested mitigations (Ethan/Maya) by 2026-03-31
Customer to provide traffic profile and sample requests for repro by 2026-04-02
Schedule controlled load test (30 min) to validate client-side retry/backoff change - target 2026-04-01
Redwood to share short-term rate-limiting profile and updated SDK config for retries (Maya) - by 2026-03-30
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we want to keep this tight 45 minutes, focus on last week's reliability event and action items. um Ethan, do you want to lead with what we saw in the logs?
[00:18] Ethan (Redwood SE): Yeah sure, so quick recap. around 18:12 UTC on 2026-03-25 we saw a spike in 5xx responses and increased tail latency. the majority were 502/504 from the gateway and a handful of 5xx from the model runtime. there's also a pattern of connection resets at the same window.
[00:37] Priya (FinStream SRE): yeah from our side we saw customer-facing timeouts, about a 10% error rate during a 20 minute window. our alerts kicked off with higher queue lengths and then a cascade of retries from the client.
[00:55] Daniel (Platform): one detail - our autoscaler didn't spin up fast enough for the burst, we had some min-replica floor set low to save cost. i think that combined with many clients retrying made the spike worse.
[01:14] Ethan: exactly, two concurrent mechanisms: provisioning gap + retry storm. also noticed some long tail requests to long-context models - seq len was higher which increased per-token work.
[01:31] Laura (Head of ML): to confirm - are these the redwood dedicated endpoints or hosted? we set the poc on dedicated with a small pool.
[01:40] Maya: it's on Redwood Dedicated (they laughed), sorry, the poc is on Dedicated pool with autoscale policies set to conservative.
[01:48] Alex (Product): there were also a few spikes in concurrent conversational sessions from a marketing campaign at 18:00 that probably drove the initial surge.
[01:57] Ethan: initial log breakdown: ~65% gateway 502/504, 25% model runtime 5xx (OOM-ish traces in some samples), 10% connection resets/timeouts. we pulled traces into the diagnostic sheet - link shared in chat (drive.google.com/finstream/poc/diag). some of the runtime 5xx messages show KV cache thrashing and increased memory usage.
[02:25] Priya: the OOM traces worry me. we run other workloads in the same pool - is there any noisy neighbor or scheduling thd?
[02:34] Ethan: we saw a few colocation events; i.e. another tenant's larger batch jobs overlapped when our pool was scaling. on Dedicated we recommend strict isolation or pinning for production - for the POC we kept cost-savings config but can change.
[02:52] Maya: ok immediate mitigations discussed: 1) temporary rate-limit per API key for the spike window, 2) adjust client-side retry/backoff to exponential with jitter to avoid synchronized retries, 3) pin heavier models to separate pool or enable burst capacity.
[03:10] Laura: for the short term the rate-limit sounds fine. how disruptive is changing retry behavior in our clients?
[03:18] Ethan: small changes. we will share suggested SDK patch and configuration (e.g., retries=3, base_backoff=200ms, max_backoff=5s, jitter=full). also recommend using idempotency keys on critical requests.
[03:34] Daniel: do you have a concrete rate limit profile? like requests/sec per key?
[03:39] Maya: propose a temporary cap at 20 rps per key for the spike window, with burst allowance up to 50 for 10s. it's conservative but should keep latency SLO intact while we investigate.
[03:52] Priya: ok we'll try that. can you also share the gateway logs for the 18:12 window? our telemetry is sampled and might not have full traces.
[04:00] Ethan: yes we'll aggregate full nginx/gateway + model runtime logs and anonymize tenant IDs per compliance. we'll put them in the diagnostic folder.
[04:10] Laura: on root cause - sounds like interplay of autoscale lag + retries + a noisy neighbor + heavier seq len. any other hypotheses?
[04:21] Ethan: also saw some mis-configured keepalive/timeouts in your LB which can amplify connection resets; some clients closed connections early and retried. once we repro, we'll test a config change.
[04:34] Maya: we also want to validate whether quantization or certain model variants were producing slower kernels at high seq len, which increases latency.
[04:43] Laura: how do you recommend we repro this safely? we don't want to cause customer impact.
[04:49] Maya: schedule a controlled window with limited traffic, maybe with synthetic sessions that mirror the campaign's payloads. Redwood can join to observe and throttle.
[04:58] Alex: preferred morning slot for us is 2026-04-01 14:00 PT.
[05:04] Maya: noted - Laura will confirm.
[05:07] Ethan: on long-term fixes: 1) increase min-replicas or faster scale-up policy for critical pools; 2) enable burst capacity with warm standby nodes; 3) model pinning; 4) improved telemetry on KV cache eviction and memory usage for early alerts.
[05:25] Daniel: what's the cost delta for reserving pinning vs current config?
[05:29] Maya: pinning adds a predictable monthly cost - we'll put numbers in the pricing note. for POC we suggested a short-term increase to cover repro and validation.
[05:39] Priya: regulatory question - logs we share, will they have any PII? we need redaction guidance.
[05:46] Sofia (CSM): we'll scrub PII and share how we handle KMS/HSM keys in Private deployments if needed. we'll mark logs as redacted and provide an audit checklist.
[05:58] Laura: ok good.
[06:01] Ethan: quick note about retries - if clients do naive immediate retries you create a retry storm. our default SDK has backoff but many in-house clients were using simple loops.
[06:12] Maya: action items recap: Ethan will gather logs, Maya will send retry config + temporary rate-limit, Priya will provide traffic CSV, Laura will set repro window.
[06:23] Alex: one more ask - can Redwood share a short runbook we can import into our incident channels?
[06:29] Maya: yes, we'll share a lightweight runbook and a checklist for triage. link: https://redwood.ai/runbooks/reliability-poc (note: internal link).
[06:38] Laura: also please include the specific metric thresholds we should alert on to catch autoscale lag earlier.
[06:44] Ethan: we'll include queue length, model runtime CPU/mem, gateway 5xx rate, and kv-cache eviction rate.
[06:52] Priya: for the controlled load test, would Redwood run with you on-call? we might want live tuning.
[06:57] Maya: yes we'll have Ethan and me on the call.
[07:01] Daniel: ok that sounds good. any other blockers?
[07:04] Laura: none from me.
[07:06] Maya: great, we'll follow up with artifacts. thanks everyone.
[07:10] (meeting ends)
